Whole Eagle Distributors Inc.  
Notes to Financial Statements 
Note 1 - Summary of Significant Accounting Policies 
Whole Eagle Distributors Inc. (the Company) is a Pennsylvania-headquartered wholesale beer distributor. The Company 
operates in the beverage alcohol three-tier system and maintains exclusive Anheuser-Busch distribution rights in select 
Southeastern Pennsylvania counties. Sales are generated primarily from domestic premium beer, supported by craft beer, 
flavored malt beverages, hard seltzers, and non-alcoholic offerings. 
The accompanying financial statements are fictitious and prepared on the accrual basis of accounting in a manner generally 
consistent with U.S. GAAP presentation. Management uses estimates and assumptions affecting reported balances and 
disclosures; actual results could differ from those estimates. 
Cash and cash equivalents include demand deposits and highly liquid instruments with original maturities of three months or 
less. 
Trade receivables are stated net of an allowance for expected credit losses. The Company generally extends short-term credit 
to retailers, bars, restaurants, and other licensed customers. 
Inventories are stated at the lower of cost or net realizable value, with cost determined using the FIFO method. Inventory 
primarily includes beer, flavored malt beverages, hard seltzers, non-alcoholic beverages, and packaging/point-of-sale materials. 
Property, plant, and equipment are stated at cost and depreciated on the straight-line method over estimated useful lives 
ranging from 3 to 39 years. 
Distribution rights are finite-lived intangible assets amortized on a straight-line basis over estimated useful lives of 20 to 25 
years. Goodwill is not presented in these fictitious statements. 
Revenue is recognized when control of products transfers to customers, generally upon delivery. Sales incentives, breakage, 
returns, discounts, and supplier-funded program adjustments are recorded as reductions of revenue. Freight billed to 
customers is included in sales and related outbound freight is included in operating expenses. 
The Company leases warehouse space, delivery tractors, trailers, and material-handling equipment. Right-of-use assets and 
lease liabilities are recognized at the present value of lease payments. 
The Company is assumed to be taxed as a pass-through entity for federal income tax purposes and therefore records primarily 
state income tax expense and deferred state tax balances in these fictitious statements.

Note 6 - Credit Agreement and Long-Term Debt 
The Company maintains a senior secured revolving credit facility used for seasonal working-capital needs, inventory purchases, 
and general corporate purposes. In addition, treasury management services include ACH and card-processing arrangements, 
and the Company maintains an interest rate swap to hedge a portion of variable-rate borrowings. 
At December 31, 2024 and 2023, revolving credit borrowings totaled $5,250,000 and $6,000,000, respectively. Scheduled term 
debt, excluding revolving borrowings, totaled $18,500,000 and $21,750,000 at December 31, 2024 and 2023, respectively, 
including current maturities of $3,750,000 and $3,500,000.

Page | 7  
 
Whole Eagle Distributors Inc. 
Interest expense associated with revolving and term borrowings was approximately $4,588,000 in 2024 and $4,812,000 in 
2023. The Company is assumed to be in compliance with all financial covenants at each year-end presented. 
Note 7 - Leases 
The Company leases warehouse facilities, office space, delivery vehicles, forklifts, and beverage-handling equipment under 
noncancelable operating lease arrangements expiring through 2031. 
Operating lease cost was approximately $2,401,000 in 2024 and $2,349,000 in 2023. Weighted-average remaining lease term 
was 4.1 years at December 31, 2024 and 4.6 years at December 31, 2023. Weighted-average discount rate was 4.9% in 2024 
and 4.8% in 2023. 
Note 8 - Revenue Concentration 
The Company has a meaningful concentration of sales and supplier support tied to Anheuser-Busch products and distribution 
rights. For this fictitious presentation, approximately 63% of 2024 net sales and 64% of 2023 net sales are assumed to have 
been generated from AB brands and related programs. 
No individual retail customer represented more than 10% of total net sales or accounts receivable in either year presented. 
Note 9 - Stockholders' Equity 
The Company is assumed to be closely held. Owner distributions totaled $596,000 in 2024 and $314,000 in 2023 and were 
recorded as reductions of retained earnings. 
Retained earnings increased primarily from profitable operations and moderate owner distributions during both years 
presented. 
Note 10 - Subsequent Events 
Management evaluated subsequent events through the date the fictitious statements were compiled and noted no items 
requiring adjustment or additional disclosure for purposes of this illustrative document.
